Your Lordship, I see the issue. The errors in your Cursor MCP logs show `ENOENT` (No such file or directory) when trying to run `/Users/khallmark/Desktop/Code/neurotypic-ai/magus-mark/magus-mcp`. The binary doesn't exist but we have the Go source code for it.

Your Grace,

That's a clever approach to get more insight! We can indeed modify the configuration that `magus-mcp` uses to make one of the server processes (like `filesystem`) redirect its output to log files. This way, when Cursor attempts to start it via `magus-mcp`, we can capture exactly what that server process is doing or any errors it might be outputting just before it closes.

To achieve this, we need to edit the `magus-mcp.json` file located at the root of your workspace. This is the configuration file that `magus-mcp` itself reads when it's asked to start a server. We'll change the `filesystem` server's configuration to use the `bin` runner to execute a shell command. This shell command will then run the `npx` server and redirect its output.

Here's the plan:
1.  I will modify `magus-mcp.json`.
2.  The `filesystem` server entry will be changed:
    *   Its `runner` will be set to `bin`.
    *   Its `package` (which becomes the command for the `bin` runner) will be set to `sh`.
    *   Its `args` will be set to execute the `npx` command for the filesystem server, with its stdout and stderr redirected to `mcp_filesystem_stdout.log` and `mcp_filesystem_stderr.log` respectively. These files will be created in your workspace root.

Here is the proposed change to `magus-mcp.json`:
